h: Golf, Then the Best of Bristol
p: Crazy golf brings out the competitor in everyone, so here's a tip: set the ground rules early. Decide on the maximum number of shots per hole, whether lucky bounces count and what the loser has to do. It makes for a smoother round and a lot more laughs. Booking ahead is a smart move at weekends, when slots fill quickly.

If you've got younger kids in tow, daytime sessions tend to be calmer. Adults looking for a livelier night out might prefer an evening tee time, but it's always worth checking age rules for later sessions.

Bristol has heaps to fill the rest of your day. Climb Cabot Tower on Brandon Hill for brilliant views over the city and harbour, then wander down to the waterfront for We The Curious, an interactive science centre that's great for families. Bristol Museum and Art Gallery is free to visit and home to a wide mix of art, natural history and archaeology.

For food, St Nicholas Market in the old city is packed with street food stalls and independent traders. Ashton Court Estate, across the river, has deer parks and woodland walks, and in August it hosts the Bristol International Balloon Fiesta, when hundreds of hot-air balloons fill the skies over the city. If your visit lands that weekend, expect busy roads and book everything well ahead, but the sight of the mass ascents drifting over the Avon Gorge is worth the effort.
